trustBoundary: The connected MCP client is authorised and belongs to the local trust boundary. These controls protect against mistakes, misfires, stale assumptions and unexpectedly broad operations; they do not defend against hostile code already exercising the same operating-system authority.

entries.title: The client and user remain responsible for intent and review
entries.outcome: The client should use inspection before mutation, convey elicitation failures accurately, review previews or receipts and keep each transaction to a coherent change.
entries.boundary: Roslyn Workbench supplies bounded tools, structured continuations and exact review data; it cannot determine the user's true intent.
entries.residualRisk: A mistaken but authorised approval can persist an undesirable change that satisfies all mechanical safeguards.

entries.title: Workspace mutation requires coordinated local ownership
entries.actor: Authorised MCP client, user and other local workspace editors
entries.outcome: Callers wait for recovery initialisation and avoid concurrent file edits or workspace-topology changes while non-cancellable commit application or recovery is in progress. A second Host instance sharing the same workspace remains advisory or query-only.
entries.boundary: Roslyn Workbench detects many stale-input and external-change conditions, but it does not hold an operating-system lock over every workspace file or coordinate independent Host processes.
entries.residualRisk: Uncoordinated local writers can invalidate assumptions during the narrow persistence boundary and can require recovery or manual reconciliation.

entries.title: Published operations expose bounded Host resource controls
entries.outcome: Collection defaults, Code Action reference lifetime and concurrent query count are fixed by Host configuration and reported without exposing sensitive configuration.
entries.boundary: These bounds apply to the corresponding Roslyn Workbench caches, references and query scheduling.
entries.residualRisk: Trusted Roslyn providers and build inputs can still consume substantial resources while an allowed operation executes.

entries.title: Optional compiler-impact validation fails closed
entries.outcome: When configured, commit is blocked by new compiler errors or incomplete compiler evaluation relative to the transaction baseline.
entries.boundary: The validation covers the projects and compilations affected by the staged transaction at commit time.
entries.residualRisk: It does not prove behavioural correctness, run all analysers or replace repository builds and tests.

entries.title: Interrupted persistence retains versioned recovery evidence
entries.actor: Roslyn Workbench commit and recovery services
entries.outcome: Commit persistence uses versioned durable evidence, reports unfinished states, and preserves unsupported versions rather than guessing how to recover them.
entries.boundary: The guarantee covers recovery artifacts created and read by Roslyn Workbench in its configured state directory.
entries.residualRisk: Operating-system or storage failure can still make evidence incomplete; status reports that condition for manual resolution.

entries.title: External error reporting is explicit, bounded and consent-controlled
entries.outcome: External reports use versioned bounded payloads, reviewed projection and redaction, and the configured consent policy before dispatch.
entries.boundary: The guarantee covers data prepared and submitted through the built-in reporting tools and configured dispatcher.
entries.residualRisk: An approved report intentionally leaves the local machine; the selected provider and operating environment govern it after dispatch.

entries.title: Generated-looking source follows explicit mutation policy
entries.outcome: Generated-looking checked-in source produces a bounded warning or is denied according to startup policy and reviewed path exceptions.
entries.boundary: Classification applies to source paths selected for supported transaction mutations.
entries.residualRisk: Path and source heuristics cannot identify every generated file; maintainers remain responsible for repository-specific exceptions and review.

entries.title: External plugin loading is explicit and mode-constrained
entries.outcome: External plugin discovery is disabled by default and fixed at startup. Plugin mutation tools are published only when the resolved operational policy enables source mutation.
entries.boundary: The Host controls discovery and publication. Once loaded, trusted plugins execute in process with Host authority.
entries.residualRisk: Plugins, analysers and Code Action providers are trusted code rather than sandboxed tenants and can perform effects outside MCP tool contracts.

entries.title: Agent-facing failure, status and continuation contracts are baseline-locked
entries.actor: Roslyn Workbench Host and Workspace services
entries.outcome: The generated compatibility baseline records the exact failure envelope, public error codes, status graph, enum values, required-action values and continuation mappings used by authorised clients.
entries.boundary: The contract covers the shared structured failure envelope and error-code catalogue, the models reachable from server and workspace status, and the structured required-action and continuation values returned by supported operations.
entries.residualRisk: The code describes the detected condition; clients must still present and follow the accompanying recovery guidance correctly.

loadDiagnostics.description: Project load and advisory workspace-status diagnostics.

location.description: The optional source location of the diagnostic.

snapshot.description: The exact immutable workspace snapshot associated with this location.

selector.description: The canonical selector that can resolve this source location again.

document.description: Provide exactly one of path or documentId.

project.description: Disambiguates documents with matching paths or IDs.

transaction.description: The active transaction info, when present.

revisionCount.description: Number of revisions retained in transaction history.

maxRevisions.description: Maximum number of revisions the transaction can retain.

remainingRevisions.description: Number of additional revisions that can be staged.

canMutate.description: Whether mutation tools may stage another change.

canUndo.description: Whether transaction history can move to the preceding revision.

canRedo.description: Whether transaction history can move to the following revision.

canCommit.description: Whether the staged transaction can be committed to disk.

canRollback.description: Whether the complete staged transaction can be discarded.

externalChange.description: The first detected external Workspace input change, when present.

detectionSource.description: The mechanism that detected the change.

errorCode.description: The stable error classification when change detection itself failed.

path.description: The affected path, when the detection mechanism identified one.

previousPath.description: The previous path for a rename, when present.

instances.description: Other live Roslyn Workbench MCP instances using this workspace.

instanceId.description: Identifier of the other Roslyn Workbench server instance.

loadedPath.description: Absolute solution or project path loaded by the other instance.

workspaceRoot.description: Absolute coordination and transaction root used by the other instance.

workspaceState.description: Workspace lifecycle state reported by the other instance.

transactionRevision.description: Staged transaction revision in the other instance, when a transaction is active.

commitId.description: Durable commit identifier reported by the other instance, when a commit is active.

commitPhase.description: Advisory durable commit phase reported by the other instance, when a commit is active.

errorReportingConsent.description: The process-local error-reporting approval applying to this Workspace and epoch.

snapshot.description: Exact immutable workspace snapshot associated with the result, when available.

warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings the agent should consider.

entries.title: Startup policy fixes the published capability surface
entries.outcome: The startup-selected operational mode resolves to immutable policy primitives, and only tools permitted by that effective policy are published.
entries.boundary: Enforcement begins during Host composition and applies to the built-in tools published by that process. MCP requests cannot widen the startup policy.
entries.residualRisk: An authorised operator can restart the Host with different settings. External plugin code runs within the separately documented plugin boundary.

entries.title: Mutations remain transaction-, snapshot- and approval-bound
entries.outcome: Source mutations require an active transaction, stale snapshots are rejected, and approval-required commits use a one-use receipt bound to the exact reviewed persistence set.
entries.boundary: The guarantee covers mutations and commits routed through the supported transaction tools and lower-level transaction service.
entries.residualRisk: A user or authorised client can approve an undesirable but accurately represented change; repository review remains necessary.

entries.title: Workspace authority constrains admitted and mutable files
entries.outcome: Workspace admission, external-document handling and mutation containment are evaluated against Host-owned authority rather than client assertions.
entries.boundary: The guarantee covers workspaces and transaction persistence performed through Roslyn Workbench.
entries.residualRisk: Other local processes and trusted build inputs can change files outside this Host and can require a workspace reload.

entries.title: Roslyn Workbench is not a hostile-code sandbox
entries.outcome: Workspaces, builds, analysers, generators, Code Action providers and enabled plugins must be trusted for local execution.
entries.boundary: The server is local and stdio-based, but trusted extensions and build inputs execute with the Host process authority.
entries.residualRisk: Hostile code with the same operating-system authority can bypass application-level controls and access local data directly.
